I am willing to give my life for that which grants me ''purpose''.|The Grand Inquisitor|[[Inquisitors 1|''Inquisitors'' 1]]}} '''The Grand Inquisitor''' was the title adopted by a [[Pau'an]] [[Gender|male]] [[Jedi Knight]] who turned to the [[dark side of the Force]] and became the [[Grand Inquisitor|leader]] of the [[Inquisitorius]], a band of [[Jedi hunter]]s who served the [[Galactic Empire]]. The Grand Inquisitor was once a [[Jedi Temple Guard]] and was involved in the events surrounding the [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar|bombing]] of the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] during the [[Clone Wars]], arresting the innocent and later exonerated [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]] as well as the true culprit, [[Barriss Offee]]. After his fall to the dark side, the Grand Inquisitor was responsible for hunting down and [[Death|eliminating]] Jedi during the [[Great Jedi Purge]]. Selected by the [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]], [[Darth Sidious]] himself, for the position of Grand Inquisitor, he personally served the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], from whom he received his orders. Throughout his tenure he proved to be one of the regime's most proficient tools in eradicating the last of the [[Jedi Order]], being intimately familiar with the records of the Jedi Temple. The Grand Inquisitor took an active interest in eliminating the [[Spectres|rebel]] crew of the [[starship]] ''[[Ghost]]'', particularly the [[Jedi]] [[Kanan Jarrus]] and his Padawan, [[Ezra Bridger]]. He encountered these two Jedi on a number of occasions, including a [[Duel on Stygeon Prime]] and a [[Rescue of Tseebo|duel]] on the [[asteroid]] base [[Fort Anaxes]]. After the Grand Inquisitor and the government of [[Lothal]], from which the rebels operated, were consistently unable to eliminate the rebels, [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] arrived on Lothal to hunt for the rebels. Together, they [[Raid on the communications tower|captured]] Jarrus and hoped to use him to learn more about a larger rebel movement that was operating in the galaxy. They brought Jarrus to [[Mustafar]], where the rebels mounted a [[Action at Mustafar|rescue mission]] in [[orbit]]. During the operation, the Grand Inquisitor engaged Jarrus and Bridger in [[lightsaber combat]], and Jarrus eventually bested him. Rather than face the infamous wrath of [[Lord]] Vader for his repeated failures, the Grand Inquisitor chose to fall to his death. But despite the Inquisitor's physical death, Vader still had use for him. The [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Dark Lord]] was able to prevent the Inquisitor's spirit from passing on, instead tying it down to a [[Jedi outpost (Tempes)|Jedi outpost]] on [[Tempes]], where his spirit remained, killing all those who sought Jedi knowledge. After the Pau'an's death over Mustafar, the former [[Grand Master|Jedi Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] utilized a vision of the Grand Inquisitor as his former Jedi Temple Guard self to appear before Jarrus in the [[Lothal Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]] on Lothal. In the vision, this '''Sentinel''' warned Jarrus that Bridger could fall to the dark side, and the two engaged in a lightsaber duel. After Jarrus refused to fight any further, the Sentinel knighted Jarrus and told him he was a Jedi Knight as the Grand Inquisitor once was. After losing [[Skywalker lightsaber|his lightsaber]] in [[3 ABY]], [[Luke Skywalker]] encountered the Inquisitor's spirit on Tempes. The two engaged in a duel that saw the young Skywalker come out victorious. As punishment for allowing the boy to escape, Vader refused the Pau'an's pleas to be set free from his prison, leaving him to guard the outpost for what the Inquisitor believed would be an eternity. ==Biography== ===Early life and knighthood=== {{Quote|The Grand Inquisitor. He had skills. He was ''trained'', at some point. Who is he?''"
"''A Jedi, once. Resentful that someone with his skill was not allowed access to the higher councils, the greater secrets of the Order.|Darth Vader and Darth Sidious|}} [[File:Sentinel.png|thumb|left|250px|The Grand Inquisitor was originally a Jedi Knight and a guardian of the sacred Jedi Temple on Coruscant.]] The Force-sensitive [[Pau'an]] [[Gender|male]] who would one [[Standard day|day]] become the [[Grand Inquisitor]] [[Homeworld|hailed]] from the [[planet]] [[Utapau]], where he was [[Reproduction|born]] over fifteen [[Standard year|years]] prior to the [[Invasion of Naboo]]. At some point, he became a member of the [[Jedi Order]] and rose to the rank of [[Jedi Knight]]. As a [[Jedi]], he served in the [[Jedi Temple Guard]], a group of Jedi tasked with defending the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]].{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}} During his time as a Jedi Knight, the Jedi proved himself a skilled individual. The knight eventually developed a hatred [[Jedi Code|unbecoming of a Jedi]], for [[Chief Librarian]] [[Jocasta Nu]]; Despite his level of skill, the Jedi was annoyed with the repressiveness of the Order, being denied access to the deeper secrets of the Force, particularly the dark side. When he would go to the [[Jedi Archives]] as he served the order, he was denied access by the elder Jedi most of the time. When he was allowed to read some [[datafile]]s on occasions, he was watched closely by her, as she deemed him as unfit for education.[[Darth Vader (2017) 7|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 7]] ===Trial of Ahsoka Tano=== [[File:BarrissInCourt-TWJ.png|thumb|right|300px|The future Grand Inquisitor was one of the Jedi Temple Guards who brought Barriss Offee before Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine.]] During the [[Clone Wars]], in a period of protests against the [[Jedi High Council]] for their continued leadership over the war between the [[Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], a [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar|bombing]] at the Jedi Temple rocked the Jedi Order.{{TCW|Sabotage (episode)}} Although the true culprit was [[Padawan]] [[Barriss Offee]], who believed that the Jedi Order had lost its way and were the true villains in the war against the Confederacy, she framed her friend and fellow Padawan [[Ahsoka Tano]] for the crime. Tano fled into the [[Coruscant Underworld]], away from the [[Grand Army of the Republic]] forces that pursued her, but she was eventually captured and brought to the Jedi Temple. She was brought before the Jedi Council, who stripped her of her Padawan status and expelled her from the Jedi Order. The future Grand Inquisitor was one of the guardsmen who led Tano from the Jedi Temple,{{WebCite|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/lukethompson/2016/03/29/review-star-wars-rebels-season-finale-non-spoiler-and-the-inquisitors-past-revealed|text=Reaction: 'Star Wars Rebels' Season Finale [Non-Spoiler], And The Inquisitor's Past Revealed|author=Thompson, Luke Y.|work=[[Wikipedia:Forbes|Forbes]]|archivedate=20200131114328}} and she was ultimately brought to [[Trial of Ahsoka Tano|trial]] before [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]]. During the trial, Tano's master, Jedi Knight [[Anakin Skywalker]], [[Duel at the Jedi Temple|uncovered]] Offee's duplicity and had her arrested. The future Grand Inquisitor was one of the guards who escorted Offee into the trial,''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' where she admitted her guilt in front of the chancellor and was subsequently taken away by the guards. Tano was exonerated, but she refused to rejoin the Jedi Order and chose to seek a new path.{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano}} ===Fall to the dark side=== {{Quote|You do know the Emperor ''personally'' selected me, Vader? Raised me up, gave me this position. He ''believes'' in my ability.|The Grand Inquisitor, to Darth Vader|}} [[File:Swi30_preview.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The former Jedi Temple Guard became an Inquisitor after turning to the dark side of the Force.]] The events with Offee and Tano left the future Grand Inquisitor feeling disaffected, and he lost faith in the Jedi Order. This left him susceptible to the pull of the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]] of [[the Force]], and ultimately fell to the dark side. However, the Pau'an was still a Jedi by the time the Clone Wars ended, as he was a survivor of [[Order 66]]. At the end of the war, the Supreme Chancellor—secretly the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth]] Sidious—[[Proclamation of the New Order|transformed]] the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire]] and declared himself [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] of [[the galaxy]].{{Film|III}} During this time, the [[Emperor]] recruited him to become Grand Inquisitor of the [[Inquisitorius]] when he promised the Jedi Knight the chance to read through the secrets of the Jedi Archives.''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side]]'' As Grand Inquisitor, he led other members of the Inquisitorius. Among these Inquisitors were dark warriors such as the [[Second Sister]], the [[Fifth Brother]],{{Rebels|Always Two There Are}} the [[Sixth Brother]],[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']] the [[Seventh Sister]], the [[Eighth Brother]],{{Rebels|Twilight of the Apprentice}} the [[Ninth Sister]], and the [[Tenth Brother]].[[Darth Vader (2017) 14|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 14]] Like the Grand Inquisitor, these Inquisitors had their roots in the Jedi Order. ===Servant of an empire=== ====Serving Lord Vader==== {{Quote|Your task is to search the Archives for clues as to where surviving Jedi might be now. Personal information…family connections. Anything. Do not delay. Do not allow yourself to become distracted. Do not ''fail''.''"
"''Don't worry, Vader. I've waited my whole life for this.|Darth Vader and the Grand Inquisitor|}} [[File:VaderVSGrandInquisitor-2017DarthVader6.png|thumb|right|250px|Not knowing each other, the Grand Inquisitor briefly dueled with his future master.]] Though the Inquisitor came into the service of the Empire and the [[Sith]], he was not a Sith himself. When the Inquisitor entered the Jedi Temple's Archives, he was [[Duel in the former Jedi Temple|confronted]] by the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth]] Vader, who was once Anakin Skywalker before his own fall to the dark side. He and the [[cyborg]] then fought each other until the latter damaged his [[The Grand Inquisitor's lightsaber|lightsaber]]. The fight was then stopped by the Emperor, who explained to [[Lord]] Vader who the Inquisitor and the Inquisitorius were. They then went to the [[Inquisitorius Headquarters]] in [[The Works]], where the Grand Inquisitor introduced Vader to the other Inquisitors as their new master. Vader then tasked the Inquisitor with hunting down and eliminating any Jedi who had survived Order 66, the order given to the [[clone trooper]]s of the Grand Army of the Republic to destroy the Jedi Order. To accomplish this task, the Inquisitor was trained in the ways of the dark side and studied the records of the Jedi Temple in order to better know his enemies.{{Rebels|Rise of the Old Masters}} Seeing how his new master employed brutal training methods that resulted in the loss of limbs from various of his Inquisitors, the Grand Inquisitor questioned Vader's methods, but the Sith Lord responded by saying that he was teaching loss to the Inquisitors and that they still fought like Jedi. After some arguing, The Grand Inquisitor reminded Vader the if the Inquisitors were to fail, said failure would be reflected on him as the Emperor appointed him to train them. As he and his master arrived at the former Jedi Temple, the Grand Inquisitor confided in Lord Vader about his hatred for Jedi Master Jocasta Nu as she denied him full access to the Jedi Archives. Now with a high ranking position at the Empire, the Grand Inquisitor claimed that he would read through everything in the Jedi Archives. Vader then assigned him to track down of any remaining Jedi survivors, a task the Inquisitor assured his master that he would not fail. ====Hunting Jocasta Nu==== {{Quote|I used to dream of this, you know. Striking you down. I thought it would be so ''easy''. After all, they didn't stick you in the library because of your ''combat skills''. Before the Purge, I could never find a way to do it—the other Jedi would have stopped me. But now…there ''are'' no other Jedi.|The Grand Inquisitor, whilst dueling Jocasta Nu|[[Darth Vader (2017) 9|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 9]]}} Unbeknownst to the Inquisitor, Jocasta Nu had infiltrated the Jedi Temple in hopes of retrieving a holocron with a list of every Force-sensitive child catalogued prior to Order 66. While the Inquisitor was unaware of Nu's presence, as he was poring over the Jedi archives, the Jedi Master soon revealed herself to him, claiming that he had no right to read her books nor toss them aside.[[Darth Vader (2017) 8|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 8]] [[File:DarthVaderSavesJocastaNu-2017DarthVader9.png|thumb|left|250px|Despite defeating Jocasta Nu, the Inquisitor was prevented from killing her by Vader.]] Held at bladepoint, The Grand Inquisitor soon revealed to Nu that he was once a Jedi who she denied access to her books even when they were on the same side, though the Inquisitor soon whipped out his own lightsaber and started a duel with the Jedi Master. During their brief duel, the Grand Inquisitor explained to Nu why he left the Jedi Order and told her that he had dreamed of striking her down for a long time. The Grand Inquisitor gained the upper hand during the duel and defeated Jocasta by knocking her to the ground, but he was prevented from killing the Jedi Master by Darth Vader, who claimed that he did not wish for her to be executed; in reality Vader was carrying the Emperor's orders of not to share information about Master Nu's importance. While the two argued, Nu took advantage of their distraction to hurl several holobooks at her opponents with the Force, which knocked the Grand Inquisitor unconscious. Vader eventually carried the hunt for Jocasta and killed her.[[Darth Vader (2017) 10|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 10]] At some point, the Grand Inquisitor assigned the [[Fifth Brother]] the task of killing his first Jedi. The Inquisitor succeeded without flaw, providing him a sense of validation.''[[Star Wars Jedi: Battle Scars]]'' ====Acquainting Akaris==== {{Quote|Here among the Inquisitorius, you will whet your skills against those of your brothers and sisters. You will seek the answers that have been kept from you, study the darkest depths of what the Force can do. You will learn that you can only harness your truest strength when you fully embrace your power and don't hold back. Even now, you didn't fully commit, but that Jedi reticence won't last long. If you don't rise to my expectations…well, you won't survive long enough to worry.''"
"''Who are you?''"
"''I'm the Grand Inquisitor, and for the foreseeable future, I'm the one you will want to impress.|The Grand Inquisitor and Iskat Akaris|}} [[File:IskatAkaris.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Iskar Akaris would soon join the Inquisitorius as the Thirteenth Sister]] On Coruscant, the Grand Inquisitor was brought the [[Pkorian]] [[Thirteenth Sister|Iskat Akaris]] by clone troopers aboard a shuttle. Presenting Akaris her lightsabers, the Inquisitor asked the former Jedi whether she was ready to abandon her past in favor of a future of her own making, to which she agreed. The Inquisitor welcomed Akaris to the Inquisitorius and drew his own saber as a challenge. Circling Akaris, he parried her strikes easily, toying with and verbally mocking her. Akaris questioned the nature of the Inquisitorius and, as the Grand Inquisitor began to explain, shoved the Pau'an back with the Force. The Inquisitor discarded his cape and informed her that the Jedi were almost extinct, recounting Mace Windu's attempt on Chancellor Palpatine's life and Order 66. The Pkorian wondered aloud how the Inquisitor knew about her and the truth about her mother, knowledge the Inquisitor taunted his opponent with, claiming that Akaris had to earn it. Akaris switched to a technique she had learned from [[Kelleran Beq]], which the Inquisitor blocked before disengaging. Deactivating his weapon, the Inquisitor declared that Akaris' performance was sufficient and properly introduced himself. Akaris hurled her first lightsaber at him, causing the Inquisitor to destroy it and bind Akaris in place with the Force, reminding her that she had much to learn before letting her go and walking away. ====Mission to Bar'leth==== {{Quote|If you wish this Gamodar to remain alive, you will convince him to open his safe. If not, I will destroy him and take what I wish.''"
"''I understand, Grand Inquisitor.''"
"''Impress me, and things will go well. Disappoint me at your peril.|The Grand Inquisitor and Iskat Akaris|}} Some time later, the Grand Inquisitor approached Akaris while she was performing calisthenics and, leading her to a landing pad, informed her of an assignment to visit [[Gamodar]], an [[Ortolan]] trader she had visited on [[Bar'leth]] alongside her Jedi Master, Sember Vey, in search of relics. Boarding the [[Scythe (Phi-class)|''Scythe'']], a [[Phi-class shuttle|''Phi''-class shuttle]],''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'' the pair set off at once. The Grand Inquisitor piloted the ship, making it clear by his demeanor that he did not wish to be disturbed. Upon arrival, Akaris questioned whether their task was a common one for the Inquisitorius, to which the Inquisitor replied that the organization itself was uncommon, tasked with taking possession of what once belonged to the Jedi. [[File:Unlimited-GrandInquisitor.png|thumb|left|300px|The Grand Inquisitor]] The Inquisitor set down at Gamodar's shop and inquired about the trader. Akaris, though reluctant, relayed what she knew, including Gamodar's security measures and the likely location of his relics within a safe. The Grand Inquisitor instructed Akaris to convince to open the safe, threatening to end the Ortolan's life should she disappoint him and departing the ship. Gamodar happily reunited with Akaris. When the shop keeper, unfamiliar with the Inquisitors, asked whether they were keepers of the peace, the Grand Inquisitor indicated that the answer was circumstantial, prompting Akaris to directly ask Gamodar for the artifacts that the duo sought. Gamodar relented and returned to his shop, only to release his security droid, Lump, on his guests. Akaris destroyed it with her lightsaber, and the Grand Inquisitor ordered her to retrieve the relics or die alongside the Ortolan as well. The Inquisitor waited and, after Akaris ultimately murdered Gamodar, was pleased when she returned with a red, triangular holocron, revealing it to be the item that he had sought specifically. The Inquisitor told Akaris to bring the rest before striding back to the ship, which she did. Upon their return to Coruscant, the Grand Inquisitor led Akaris into a chamber within Inquisitorius Headquarters where she was officially inducted into the Inquisitorius; Akaris swore allegiance to the Inquisitor and his masters and received the title Thirteenth Sister, though she did not yet wish to use it. ====Akaris' independence==== {{Quote|News has reached us of two rogue Jedi hiding on Firrhana. You will travel to the Outer Rim, root them out, and destroy them. Do you understand?''"
"''Yes, Grand Inquisitor.''"
"''Look at me child. This is your first real mission. It is one thing to realize that the Jedi are the enemy, but it is another thing entirely to participate in their necessary eradication. Do not give them a chance to speak, to poison you with their rhetoric, for they will attempt to sway you with their weak persuasion and pathetic mewling. You are a Jedi no longer.|The Grand Inquisitor and Iskat Akaris|}} [[File:Camtono.jpg|thumb|right|245px|Iskat Akaris retuned with a camtono (a camtono pictured).]] Subsequent to the mission to Bar'leth, the Grand Inquisitor halted a duel between Akaris and the Seventh Sister. The Inquisitor summoned Akaris after she returned from an expedition of self-discovery to her homeworld of Pkori, to ask what she had learned. Akaris relayed the truth of her past, which the Grand Inquisitor expressed it was foolish of the Jedi to keep from her. The Pau'an inquired as to the nature of the [[camtono]] Akaris had brought with her, supposing it to be another relic. Akaris informed him that the device, which she had acquired the device from Morgest, another of Vey's associates, on Takodana, did contain an artifact—a lightsaber. The Grand Inquisitor summoned the weapon to his hand, inspected it, and praised Akaris for returning with a boon to diminish the waste of his time before dismissing her. The Grand Inquisitor sent for Akaris again after a lightsaber wound from her former friend and fellow Inquisitor [[Tualon Yaluna]] landed her in the medbay for the third time, the [[RA-7 protocol droid]] [[6-RA-7]] instructing the Pkorian to report to the Grand Inquisitor's chambers. There, he sat upon his throne and asked Akaris whether she was recovered from her latest injury. Akaris shortly confirmed that she had, having learned that that was the only right answer. The Inquisitor then gave Akaris her first true mission, to investigate and destroy two rogue Jedi on the Outer Rim world of [[Firrhana]], and warned her not to be swayed by her enemies' words, rhetoric he considered to be "weak persuasion" and "pathetic mewling." Akaris inquired as to the names of the Jedi, which the Inquisitor dismissed as unimportant, as they were all traitors. The Inquisitor then sent her on her way, Akaris promising not disappoint him. The Grand Inquisitor awaited Akaris in his chambers alongside Darth Vader. Akaris returned, and the Inquisitor inquired as to the Pkorian's success, which she affirmed by placing three lightsabers before him. Vader praised Akaris, to which she rejected the name, embracing her new identity as the Thirteenth Sister. ====An evaluation on Nur==== {{Quote|I must confess, you've impressed us. You both have. Unfortunately, there is only room in our ranks for one. And so, you must face one final test.''"
''''[The Grand Inquisitor produces a lightsaber]''''
"''You may choose not to fight, of course. In which case, both of you will die.|The Grand Inquisitor, to Barriss Offee and Dante|{{TOTE|Devoted}}}} On Nur, the Grand Inquisitor introduced himself to [[Ahmar]], [[Dante]], and [[Barriss Offee]], three former Jedi brought before him by [[Fourth Sister]], at [[Fortress Inquisitorius]]. Questioned by Offee, he informed them of fall of the Jedi and the reorganization of the Republic into the first Galactic Empire. Citing the need for order, the Inquisitor informed the trio that the prospect of protecting the Emperor's vision lay before them before sending the Jedi to their quarters and advising them not to leave. [[File:Devoted-TotE.png|thumb|left|250px|Barriss Offee trained with the Grand Inquisitor, who administered her final test.]] Ahmar later tried to escape. Dante and Offee were subsequently brought before the Inquisitor, who informed them that their companion had suffered an "accident" and, after dismissing the Fourth Sister and Dante, took Offee aside to train. Proceeding to a hidden chamber, the Grand Inquisitor lectured Offee on the limitations of her Jedi training and presented her with a lightsaber. Instructing Offee to attack him, the Inquisitor easily evaded her strikes. The Pau'an told Offee to embrace her anger, leading her to strike him. The Inquisitor then praised Offee before retaliating, calling upon the Force to violently throw his opponent against the ceiling. Further goading caused Offee to push the Inquisitor into a wall in retaliation, bloodying the Pau'an and earning a smirk. The Grand Inquisitor, impressed with both Dante and Offee, oversaw a final duel between the pair. Offee, initially reluctant to fight, strangled her opponent to death with the Force, earning her a place amongst the Inquisitorius. The Pau'an was later present alongside Fourth Sister, Offee, [[Marrok|First Brother]], and the [[Eleventh Brother]] for the arrival of Darth Vader. The Inquisitors knelt before their master until the Grand Inquisitor rose and ordered the others to stand as well, proclaiming the phrase "[[long live the Empire]]." ====Later missions==== {{Quote|Kira Vantala. I admit that I'm surprised. Of all those who might have survived the purge…I did not imagine a weakling such as you to be among them.''"
"''Then that was your mistake, for the dark side has forever underestimated me.|The Grand Inquisitor and Kira Vantala|{{StoryCite|story=The Orphanage (short story)|book=Dark Legends}}}} At some stage, the Grand Inquisitor would also trained [[Reva Sevander|Third Sister]], improving both her skills in [[Jar'Kai]] and teaching her a aggressive version of his preferred [[Form II]].{{AtomicMassGames|url=transmission/databank-download-grand-inquisitor-fallen-jedi-third-sister-preview|text=Databank Download: Grand Inquisitor, Fallen Jedi & Third Sister Preview}} However, he maintained a low opinion of her abilities. At one point during his service to the Empire, the Inquisitor embarked on a quest for answers that involved him tracking down a bearded human. As the man hid, the Inquisitor pursued with his lightsaber ignited.{{FFGTCG|set=Promise of Power|cardname=Press for Answers|link=alliances-cycle/promise-of-power/press-for-answers-r2114}} [[File:TheOrphanage.jpg|thumb|right|240px|The Grand Inquisitor abducted children from an orphanage on Gaaten.]] One Jedi that the Inquisitor led to their [[death]] was [[Jedi Master]] [[Luminara Unduli]]. After the execution of Order 66, Unduli was captured and held in the [[Spire (Stygeon Prime)|Spire]], a former Separatist[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 1|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 1]]-turned-Imperial [[prison]] on [[Stygeon Prime]]. At her end, Unduli was in the presence of the Inquisitor, who stood in the doorway of her cell as she walked into an execution chamber and died. The Inquisitor kept her remains in the prison cell, using them to lure other Jedi to their deaths when they heard rumors that Unduli was still alive. A [[Hologram|holographic]] recording of Unduli and her execution was kept by the Empire as part of this ruse. As the Grand Inquisitor, the dark side adept hunted down and dueled the former Jedi Padawan [[Naq Med]]. His lightsaber was damaged in the duel and Med escaped.''[[Force Collector]]'' At another point, the Grand Inquisitor took Force-sensitive children from an [[Gaaten orphanage|orphanage]] on [[Gaaten]]. One night when he went to the orphanage, he was confronted by a surviving Jedi, [[Kira Vantala]], to which the Grand Inquisitor expressed his shock, believing her to be a weak Jedi. The Inquisitor was defeated by Vantala and a [[refugee]] named [[Elish]], and never returned to the orphanage. ====Evidence of another survivor==== {{Quote|Set a course back to base. And inform Lord Vader that we have found evidence of another survivor.|The Grand Inquisitor, after investigating the Sixth Brother's death on Raada|}} [[File:DV16Cover-SixthBrother.jpg|thumb|left|240px|The Grand Inquisitor investigated the death of the Sixth Brother and realized it confirmed another survivor of the Great Jedi Purge.]] One year after the rise of the Galactic Empire, the Grand Inquisitor was alerted of the presence of a [[Force-sensitive]] being old enough to have received [[Jedi training]] on the [[farm]]ing [[moon]] of [[Raada]]. Though he wanted to hunt down the supposed Jedi himself, he was needed elsewhere, and the task instead went to the Sixth Brother, who then went to Raada to lay a trap for the Force-sensitive. However, he was killed in the following [[Raada Uprising|battle]], and the Jedi, as well as the [[farmer]]s who had rebelled against the recent occupation, escaped. Meanwhile, the Grand Inquisitor was alerted to the situation and traveled to the moon with a [[fleet]] of [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|Star Destroyers]] to provide backup, but by the time they arrived, the insurgents were gone. The Grand Inquisitor personally examined the damage done by the battle and discovered the corpse of the Sixth Brother. Though annoyed by the incompetence and recklessness of his subordinate, the Grand Inquisitor was impressed by what the Jedi had done. He then went back to his ship and instructed his [[agent]]s to set a course back to base and to inform Lord Vader that they had found evidence of another survivor—who was, in fact, Ahsoka Tano, Anakin Skywalker's former Padawan. ====The rogue Inquisitors==== {{Quote|We know they're out there, but there have been no signs, no signals. The Inquisitor cited the willingness of the people to defend Run, who Vader declared had become a symbol of hope. Vader recounted the conquest of Regis Kor, the raid on an Imperial outpost that made Run famous, instructing the Inquisitorius to search the far reaches of the galaxy for the fugitive. Move aside.|The Grand Inquisitor and Third Sister|{{Kenobi|Part II}}}} [[File:Grand_Inquisitor_on_Daiyu.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor interrogated Vect Nokru on Daiyu.]] After the Third Sister hired [[Vect Nokru]] and his [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] to [[Ambush on Alderaan|kidnap]] the [[Alderaanian]] [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and bring her to [[Daiyu]] in hopes that Obi-Wan Kenobi would be contacted by Leia's adoptive father, [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]], to rescue her, the Grand Inquisitor went to Daiyu accompanied by the Fifth Brother and the [[Fourth Sister]] so they could [[Hunt for Obi-Wan|capture]] Kenobi. [[File:Third_Sister_stabs_the_Grand_Inquisitor.jpg|thumb|left|250px|During their mission on Daiyu, The Grand Inquisitor was betrayed by the Third Sister.]] As they secured the city, the Grand Inquisitor requested the Fifth Brother to shut down the planet's port and request a [[garrison]] within an [[Standard hour|hour]]. As Vader walked off the bridge, the Grand Inquisitor eyed him briefly.{{Kenobi|Part VI}} ===Nemesis of the Spectres=== ====The children of the Force==== {{Quote|The Jedi Knights are all but destroyed. And yet your task is not complete, Inquisitor. The Emperor has foreseen a new threat rising against him; the children of the Force. They must not become Jedi.''"
"''Yes, Lord Vader.''"
"''Hunt down this new enemy. And if they will not serve the Empire, eliminate them along with any surviving Jedi who would train them. This is my master's command.''"
"''And so it will be done.|Darth Vader and the Grand Inquisitor|''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]''}} In the years prior to the [[Battle of Yavin]], the Grand Inquisitor was contacted by Lord Vader, who told the [[Jedi hunter]] that the Emperor had foreseen a new threat rising to challenge his rule: the "children of the Force," who could not be allowed to become Jedi. Thus, the Inquisitor was instructed to hunt these individuals down and either make them serve the Empire or destroy them, along with any Jedi survivors who could train them. With the orders of the Emperor given, the Inquisitor told his master that it would be done. [[File:Inquisitor_Speaks_to_Vader.png|thumb|left|250px|The Grand Inquisitor was ordered by Darth Vader to hunt down the "children of the Force."]] One method that the Inquisitor used to find Force-sensitive individuals was to look for [[cadet]]s at the [[Academy for Young Imperials]] on [[Lothal]] who met a set of criteria, one that indicated their ability to use the Force,{{Rebels|Breaking Ranks}} an operation known as [[Project Harvester]]. One known target of Project Harvester was [[Dhara Leonis]], a promising cadet and the daughter of Imperial agricultural scientists. The Imperial authorities attempted to cover up her kidnapping by claiming that she had run away from the Academy.''[[Servants of the Empire: Rebel in the Ranks]]'' However, her mother, [[Tepha Leonis|Tepha]], and younger brother [[Zare Leonis]] suspected that the Empire was lying. To ascertain his sister's fate, Zare enrolled at the Academy the following year.''[[Servants of the Empire: Edge of the Galaxy]]'' Sometime later, fourteen years after the rise of the Empire, a group of [[Spectres|rebels]] who operated on Lothal came to the attention of [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus]] of the [[Imperial Security Bureau]]. The rebels [[Mission to free Wookiee prisoners|rescued]] a group of [[Wookiee]]s that had been [[Slavery|enslaved]] in the [[Spice mines of Kessel|spice mines]] of [[Kessel]], a mission in which the rebel leader, [[Kanan Jarrus]], used a [[lightsaber]] and revealed himself as a Jedi survivor. After the rebels escaped, Kallus contacted the Inquisitor and informed him about what happened on Kessel. The Inquisitor was pleased that Kallus informed him of the rebel cell and the Jedi in its ranks. ====Trap on Stygeon Prime==== {{Quote|Yes, I'm afraid Master Luminara died with the Republic, but her bones continue to serve the Empire. Luring the last Jedi to their ends.|The Grand Inquisitor to Kanan Jarrus and Ezra Bridger|}} The Grand Inquisitor laid a trap for Jarrus and his Padawan, [[Ezra Bridger]], in the Spire. The Empire was able to project an image suggesting that she was alive, and this information was then reported by [[Gall Trayvis]], a former member of the [[Imperial Senate]] who claimed to have gone into exile after speaking out against the Empire—in reality, Trayvis was a loyal agent of the Empire, one who used his position to lure rebel groups into traps around the galaxy.{{Rebels|Vision of Hope}} Not wanting to pass up an opportunity to rescue a Jedi survivor, the rebels undertook a [[Duel on Stygeon Prime|mission]] to the Spire, where they intended to rescue the Jedi Master. [[File:Kanan_vs_Inquisitor.png|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor confronted Kanan Jarrus, a Jedi Padawan who survived the execution of Order 66.]] Once in the prison, the rebels fought their way through [[stormtrooper]]s who were stationed there. Jarrus and Bridger made it to the detention area, and Jarrus believed he could sense the Jedi Master—though, in actuality, it was the power from her bones. They entered the cell and saw a projected image of Unduli, which faded into a sarcophagus that revealed the remains of the Jedi Master. The Grand Inquisitor entered the cell, his lightsaber ignited, and approached the two Jedi, revealing that Luminara had been dead for many years. Jarrus attacked the Inquisitor and the two engaged in lightsaber combat. The Inquisitor was able to correctly deduce that Jarrus had been trained by Jedi Master [[Depa Billaba]], as she had been a teacher of [[Form III]] lightsaber combat in close-quarter fighting, which Jarrus employed extensively. The two continued their duel within the cell until Bridger set off a small detonator that allowed him and Jarrus to flee. Though they had escaped the cell, the Grand Inquisitor pursued them and continued his fight with Jarrus in the halls of the prison. He soon pushed Jarrus away through the Force and, per Vader's command, attempted to convert Bridger to the dark side. The boy refused, however, and the Inquisitor prepared to strike him down, but Jarrus used the Force to pin the Inquisitor to the ceiling, giving the two Jedi a chance to flee. The Grand Inquisitor followed them and chased them through the prison before they met back up with their fellow rebels. Separated by a number of closed doors, the Inquisitor sliced through them with his lightsaber and arrived in time to see the rebels beginning to escape. He made one last attempt to stop them by throwing his lightsaber towards them, but Jarrus deflected it and the rebels escaped aboard the ''[[Phantom]]'', the attack shuttle that belonged to their main ship, the ''[[Ghost]]''. ====Incident at the Imperial Academy==== {{Quote|Well, Leonis, let's take a walk, shall we? I want to know everything about your ''former'' friends.|The Grand Inquisitor, to Zare Leonis|}} [[File:The_Grand_Inquisitor_and_Zare_Leonis.png|thumb|left|250px|Zare Leonis suspected that the Grand Inquisitor was involved in the disappearance of his sister, Dhara Leonis.]] After his failure to stop the rebels on Stygeon Prime, the Inquisitor was contacted by [[Commandant]] [[Cumberlayne Aresko]], the lead officer at the Imperial Academy on Lothal, who informed him of two students who potentially met his criteria for Force-sensitivity. He learned that these cadets were Dev Morgan—who, unknown to the Academy, was Bridger in disguise, who [[Mission to destroy a kyber crystal|infiltrated]] the Academy to learn the location of a giant [[kyber crystal]] of great power—and [[Jai Kell]]. Upon his arrival at the Imperial Academy, Aresko and Agent Kallus informed him of Bridger and Kell's escape. The Jedi hunter was shown the data files on the two cadets and recognized "Dev Morgan" as Bridger from their encounter on Stygeon Prime. During his private chat with Leonis, the Inquisitor led the young cadet to an interrogation room. Once inside, the Inquisitor asked Leonis everything he knew about Morgan while trying to probe the cadet's thoughts. While hiding his collaboration with Morgan, Leonis pretended to support the Inquisitor's assessment that something was not right about Morgan. He claimed that he could somehow sense that there was something wrong with Dev and Jai and that they were hiding something. The Inquisitor quickly deduced that Leonis was Dhara's younger brother. While the Inquisitor was fully aware that Dhara had been abducted and forcibly inducted into Project Harvester, he repeated the official Imperial account that Dhara had merely run away. When Zare claimed that he and his sister could always sense each others' presence, the Inquisitor merely told the young cadet that it made sense and that in time he would understand why. ====Skirmish on Vyndal==== {{Quote|Another Jedi! This is indeed a surprise. How many more Padawans have you taken?"
"He's not my Padawan."
"Then you won't be emotionally compromised when he dies.|The Grand Inquisitor, to Kanan Jarrus about Yeleb the Protector|{{RebelsMagCite|3|The Fake Jedi}}}} The Inquisitor and his Imperial forces arrived in a [[Unidentified village (Vyndal)|village]] on the planet [[Vyndal]] in search of Jarrus after he had been seen close by. [[File:Skirmish_on_Vyndal.png|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor killed Yeleb, but failed to capture Kanan Jarrus on Vyndal.]] Jarrus revealed himself to the Inquisitor and [[Skirmish on Vyndal|attacked]] him. Yeleb would soon join the combat as well, wielding his own green-bladed lightsaber, leading the Inquisitor to assume that Yeleb was a Jedi too, although, in actual fact, a few years earlier Yeleb had taken the lightsaber from a crashed [[Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class light interceptor]] with a dead [[Unidentified Jedi (Vyndal)|Jedi]] [[pilot]] inside. After Yeleb collapsed onto the floor, the Inquisitor took Yeleb's lightsaber and Jarrus fled from the Inquisitor to draw him away from the wounded [[human]]. The Pau'an along with his stormtroopers gave chase, and Jarrus was able to trick the Imperials into thinking he had fled Vyndal on one of their [[cruiser]]s, causing them to chase after it and leave the planet in the other. After the Imperials left the planet, Yeleb died of his injuries, and Jarrus ended up leaving the planet and returning to the rebels, leaving the [[Unidentified Vyndal species|people of Vyndal]] with hope that without him and the lightsaber on the planet, the Empire would not return, and even if they did, the people were able to protect themselves. ====Empire Day==== {{Quote|I still sense the Jedi and his Padawan, within my ''grasp''.|The Grand Inquisitor|}} The Inquisitor was on Lothal for [[Empire Day]] when the rebels destroyed the prototype [[TIE/ad v1]]. When the rebels attempted to smuggle [[Tseebo]], an [[Imperial Information Office]] worker who had fled with Imperial secrets, off Lothal, he led a TIE fighter squadron while piloting his own [[The Inquisitor's TIE Advanced|TIE/ad v1]] to stop them from escaping. He was able to plant an [[XX-23 S-thread tracker]] on their ship moments before they jumped to hyperspace.{{Rebels|Empire Day (episode)}} [[File:The_Grand_Inquisitor_on_Fort_Anaxes.png|thumb|left|250px|The Grand Inquisitor tracked Jarrus and his apprentice, Ezra Bridger, to the ruins of Fort Anaxes.]] Realizing they were being tracked, Jarrus and Bridger boarded the ''Phantom'' and ejected from the ''Ghost'', flying it to [[Fort Anaxes]]. The Inquisitor took a squad of troops and its [[Unidentified stormtrooper commander (PM-1203)|commander]] with him aboard a [[Sentinel-class landing craft|''Sentinel''-class landing craft]] to confront the two Jedi. As the Inquisitor and his troopers entered the base, they spotted Jarrus and Bridger along with a multitude of [[fyrnock]]s. The two Jedi used the Force to command the fyrnocks to attack the stormtroopers. Jarrus fought the Inquisitor once more, but he was easily overwhelmed and knocked out. Cornering Bridger, the Inquisitor told him to give in to the dark side, and that his friends would die and that everything he fought for would be lost. Bridger briefly succumbed to the dark side and summoned a giant fyrnock to attack the Inquisitor. Jarrus reawakened, grabbing Bridger and reclaiming his lightsaber. After driving off the mother fyrnock, the Inquisitor attempted to halt their escape, but they managed to board their ship, the ''Phantom'', and destroy the Imperial landing craft. Accepting his failure, the Inquisitor simply stated that his [[Anakin Skywalker|master]] would not be pleased. ====Dealing with Zare Leonis==== {{Quote|Who can doubt the commitment of such a promising young cadet?|The Grand Inquisitor probing Zare Leonis|''[[Servants of the Empire: Imperial Justice]]''}} [[File:Morgan_and_Leonis_Secret_Meeting.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Grand Inquisitor suspected that Zare Leonis had secret ties to Ezra Bridger and his Lothal-based rebel cell.]] Following the Lothal rebels' attack on the Empire Day celebrations, the Grand Inquisitor returned to Lothal to deal with another unfinished business: Dhara Leonis' younger brother Zare Leonis. While Zare was a promising cadet at the Academy for Young Imperials who had earned the glowing praise of his instructors, the Inquisitor suspected that Leonis was connected to Ezra Bridger and the other Lothal rebels. A perfect opportunity to make his move against Zare surfaced when the young cadet took action against an unscrupulous fellow cadet named [[Nazhros Oleg]], who had attempted to shield his smuggler uncles from Imperial justice. Under the pretext of rewarding Leonis, the Inquisitor arranged for the cadet to be transferred to the [[Arkanis Academy]], which was connected to Project Harvester. There, he hoped to create the circumstances that would expose Leonis as a traitor to the Empire. In addition, the Inquisitor wanted to ascertain whether Zare was actually Force-sensitive as he had claimed earlier. Following Leonis' raid on a group of smugglers, the Inquisitor and [[Captain]] [[Piers Roddance]] summoned Zare for a private meeting. When Leonis suggested that Oleg was genuinely unaware that his uncles were involved in smuggling and suggested showing the delinquent some compassion, the Inquisitor replied that compassion was the most insidious business. After ordering Captain Roddance to leave the room, the Inquisitor told Leonis that he had arranged for the cadet to be transferred to the Arkanis Academy as a "reward" for his loyalty to the Empire. Throughout the meeting, the Inquisitor made every effort to probe Leonis' thoughts. Pretending to be a "model" cadet, Leonis expressed gratitude at the opportunity to serve the Empire. Sensing Leonis' true motivations for joining the Imperial Academy, the Inquisitor patronized Leonis by asking "who could doubt the commitment of such a promising young cadet." Intimidated by the Inquisitor, Leonis turned away from the Pau'an's gaze, prompting the Inquisitor to ask the cadet to make eye contact with him. Prior to Leonis' departure, the Inquisitor told the cadet that he looked forward to his training on Arkanis and "assured" the Cadet that his service to the Empire would be more important than he had hoped for. While Leonis was uncertain whether the Inquisitor knew his true agenda, his girlfriend [[Merei Spanjaf]] uncovered Imperial documents which confirmed that the Inquisitor had intended to use the Arkanis transfer to break the young cadet. Later, the Inquisitor visited the Arkanis Academy and landed at [[Area Null]], a secluded tower in the Academy that hosted several top-secret Imperial projects including Project Harvester and [[Project Unity]], the latter a program for re-educating former dissident youths. After dining with Commandant [[Brendol Hux]] and the cadets in the Academy's banquet hall, the Inquisitor summoned Cadet Leonis for a private meeting at the Commandant's balcony. There, the Inquisitor asked Leonis why he had tried to enter Area Null even though it was off-limits to Cadets. Leonis claimed that he thought that a fellow cadet was in trouble but the Inquisitor quickly realized that he was lying.''[[Servants of the Empire: The Secret Academy]]'' He then gave Leonis a second chance to answer his question. Leonis claimed that he had sensed that there was something in that tower that he was meant to find. The Inquisitor then asked if Morgan had told him about the tower on Lothal or something called Project Harvester. In response, Leonis feigned ignorance but the Inquisitor could see that he was trying to hide something. Before the Inquisitor could carry on with the interrogation, the Commandant's droid [[DDM-38]] arrived and informed him that he had received a priority encrypted message from Lothal. Before leaving, the Inquisitor warned Leonis that he would soon have Morgan and his companions. He also vowed to get to the truth behind Leonis' connection to Morgan. Unknown to the Inquisitor and Leonis, this was to be their last meeting due to unexpected developments. ====Talking with Rae Sloane==== {{Quote|Vice Admiral…''"
"''Not now, I-- *gasp*''"
"''Vice Admiral Rae Sloane, I am the ''Emperor's Grand Inquisitor''… and I want you to tell me ''everything'' you know… about your ''hobby''.|The Grand Inquisitor and Rae Sloane|[[Kanan 12|''Kanan'' 12]]}} To continue tracking the rebels, at some point the Grand Inquisitor sought information from [[Vice Admiral]] [[Rae Sloane]] of the [[Imperial Navy]]. Sloane once had a run-in with Jarrus on the planet [[Gorse]], where Jarrus first met Captain [[Hera Syndulla]] and joined her rebel cause.[[A New Dawn (novel)|''A New Dawn'']] The Grand Inquisitor found the [[officer]] on [[Lahn]], where she had set a trap for the Jedi. Jarrus escaped, but Sloane remained on Lahn when she was confronted by the Inquisitor—who wanted to know everything she knew about Jarrus. ====Visions of darkness==== {{Quote|Ready to die, boy, or are you afraid to face your demise?''"
"''No. Afraid of being alone again? Sure. Afraid of letting down my master? Absolutely.''"
